chunks: From him, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Dorust al-Wasiti, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abdul Rahman al-Qasir, who said:

I said to him, 'Does the believer visit his family?' He said, 'Yes. He seeks permission from his Lord, so He grants it. He sends two angels with him, and they come to them in one of the forms of birds, alighting in his house, looking at them, and hearing their speech.'
ai.seo_question: How does a deceased believer visit their family according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, this narration highlights the Shia belief in the continued spiritual presence of the deceased, who seeks divine permission to visit their family accompanied by two angels. The imagery of appearing in the form of birds (*surat al-tayr*) suggests a subtle, non-physical manifestation that allows the soul to observe and listen to the living without being fully perceived, emphasizing the enduring bond between the departed and the bereaved.
